You can use any other functions too. As baseline.sstable has been formated in flextable format by argument flextable = TRUE. baseline.sstable # a label is simply a "label" attribute (Hmisc::label() sets the same attribute) baseline_data <- baseline_data %>%   mutate(     age = structure(age, label='Age'), #label to make capital letter     sex = structure(sex, label='Sex'),     bmi = structure(bmi, label='Body Mass Index'), #label to explain the variable     tetanus = structure(tetanus, label='Tetanus Confirmation'),     icudays = structure(icudays, label='Days in ICU'),     outcome = structure(outcome, label='Outcome'),     timetoadm = structure(timetoadm, label='Time to Admission'),     maxtemp = structure(maxtemp, label='Max Temperature'),     resp = structure(resp, label='Respiratory Rate'),     fio2 = structure(fio2, label='FiO2'),     spo2 = structure(spo2, label='SpO2'),     pao2 = structure(pao2, label='PaO2'),     wbc = structure(wbc, label='White Blood Cells'),     sofa = structure(sofa, label='SOFA')   )  baseline_data$sex <- factor(baseline_data$sex, levels = c( "M", "F"), labels = c( "Male", "Female"))  baseline.sstable <- sstable.baseline(   formula = age + sex + bmi + tetanus + icudays + outcome + timetoadm +             maxtemp + resp + fio2 + spo2 + pao2 + wbc + sofa ~ Arm,   data = baseline_data,   pooledGroup = FALSE,   flextable = TRUE,   footer = "we can add any note here and it will appear at the bottom of the table",   bg = "lightblue") %>% set_caption(caption = 'Baseline characteristics of study population grouped by Treatment Arm.')  baseline.sstable baseline.sstable <- sstable.baseline(   formula = age + sex + bmi + tetanus + icudays + outcome + timetoadm +             maxtemp + resp + fio2 + spo2 ~ Arm,   data = baseline_data,   pooledGroup = TRUE, #column total is added   flextable = TRUE,   fullfreq = TRUE, # as you can see in the table above in in intrathecal group female was shown as 22, but in the table below female is being shown as 22/136.   footer = "we can add any note here and it will appear at the bottom of the table",   bg = "lightblue")  library(flextable) baseline.sstable <- baseline.sstable %>%   set_caption(caption = 'Baseline characteristics of study population grouped by Treatment Arm.')  baseline.sstable # title: Summary Tables and Tools for Clinical Trial Reporting
text: independently maintained version C306, based oucru-biostats/C306. C306 collects R tools used Biostatistics group Oxford University Clinical Research Unit (OUCRU) analyse report clinical studies: report tables: baseline characteristics, adverse events, time--event comparisons (Cox, Fine–Gray, restricted mean survival time, cumulative incidence), overall subgroup, flextables (Word, HTML, PDF) plain matrices; model summaries: odds ratios likelihood-ratio Wald CIs, also within subgroups interacting variable; plots: Aalen–Johansen curves competing risks, Box–Cox profile likelihood; data tools: import OUCRU data dictionary, format raw data , check data missing --range values.

title: C306 0.2.0
text: Five bugs gave wrong numbers tables plots. Reports made periods affected arguments re-run version. case, numbers table correct. Functions: sstable.survcomp(), sstable.survcomp.subgroup() (rows), tables built (ss_flextable(), ss_huxtable(), rbind()). Affected: add.risk = TRUE (default), compare.method. sstable.survcomp.subgroup() always uses . Period: 2024-07-09 (upstream oucru-biostats/C306 commit 40aeabd, “Adding mstate model survcomp”; versions 0.1.5-022405 0.1.5-240715) version. wrong: “risk [%]” figure 100 × cumulative hazard, absolute risk (e.g. 232% instead 92%). now 1 − Kaplan–Meier, Aalen–Johansen probability cause interest competing risks. Competing-risks tables wrong start (commit). 2024-07-09 column correct. Event counts, HRs, RMST/cumulative-incidence estimates, CIs p-values affected. Function: sstable.survcomp.subgroup(). Affected: reference.arm = "", subgroup rows (“patients”). Period: 2024-06-17 (upstream oucru-biostats/C306 commit cbe10dc, reference.arm added) version. wrong: subgroup rows ignored reference.arm always used arm B reference, HR / RMST / cumulative-incidence comparisons inverted relative “patients” row (e.g. HR 0.54 shown instead 1.85). Function: sstable.survcomp.subgroup(). Affected: compare.method = "rmst" "cuminc" model.censoring given compare.args; “Test heterogeneity” p-value . Period: 2024-06-13 (upstream oucru-biostats/C306 commit 869429c, “add RMST survcomp”) version. wrong: user’s model.censoring replaced eventglm default ("independent") interaction test, heterogeneity p-value used different censoring model one requested (e.g. 0.795 instead 0.375). Function: subgroup_effect(), including sstable = TRUE, flextable = TRUE transpose = TRUE output. Affected: calls, method = "lik.ratio" "wald"; CI.lower / CI.upper columns . Period: 2019-12-26 (upstream oucru-biostats/C306 commit 5b44416, function added) version. wrong: CI log odds ratio, printed next odds ratio (e.g. 1.06 “CI” (-0.20, 0.32) instead (0.82, 1.37)). now CI , logist_summary(). ORs, log ORs p-values correct. Functions: gg_ajsurvplot() (2024-06-20, upstream oucru-biostats/C306 commit 17a757d) gg_ajsurvplot2(), including .return_data = TRUE (2024-06-25, upstream commit b89f64b), version. Affected: plots groups right-hand side formula whose censoring patterns differ. wrong: censoring weights pooled groups, curves Aalen–Johansen estimate group. drifted late follow-(2.5 percentage points survival::mgus2 sex). Early follow-essentially unchanged. curves now exact Aalen–Johansen estimates. Fine–Gray hazard ratios sstable.survcomp() affected (correctly use pooled weights).
